notes.title: Devlog #7: The Drone That Will Save Your Life
notes.content:
[h1]Welcome![/h1]

[h3]Another devlog, more news! A new companion in Tarvos – a drone that fights by your side![/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057663/f76f3e5786742f62cb20f666b5551c7cc71c28b3.gif[/img]

Our drone has just received its final texture version. It’s not a shiny gadget fresh from the factory – its surface shows signs of wear, as if it remembers abandoned laboratories and the weight of Tarvos’s industrial world. Thanks to this, it will not only blend into the dark atmosphere but also become a believable part of the environment. It’s equipment that players will encounter in the full version of the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057663/82b8d6b3250a3527e79285d42f7ac7868f2c89ea.png[/img]

[h1]The Drone as the Player’s Companion[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057663/75b44b8cb1b1605db6687197cc82aa297af1844d.jpg[/img]

But the drone’s usefulness doesn’t end with blending into the dark setting – from the very beginning, we planned for it to become an active companion. Hovering by the player, it will:

[list]
[*] Lock onto enemies: instantly identifies threats and warns the player.
[*] Provide fire support: opens fire, distracting opponents and giving you a moment to counterattack.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057663/609c554c1e930b4044f6be546323ad296c04868c.gif[/img]

Imagine exploring ruined corridors as the drone quietly flashes its sensors, fires precise shots, and lets the player focus on survival and tactics – the drone becomes an ally and… a living part of the world.

[h1]What’s Next?[/h1]

The next step is to adjust the AI to dynamic combat situations and test how the drone reacts to the chaos of battle – whether it truly helps or still needs fine-tuning so it doesn’t distract the player.

[h1]Thanks for being with us![/h1]

We hope this quick insight into our work on the drone brought you a little closer to our daily life as developers and the atmosphere we’re aiming for. What do you think about the drone as a companion? What extra feature would you give it? Share your ideas in the comments and don’t forget to add Tarvos Desolation to your wishlist if you haven’t already – it’s the best way to help us keep growing the game!

notes.title: Devlog #6: Safe House
notes.content:
Hi! In today’s devlog, we’ll take a look at the new feature we’ve introduced to the world of Tarvos: Desolation.

[h3][b]Safe House:[/b][/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057663/f19229c0a172d361f78ffd807934cffc6749efec.gif[/img]

[b]What can you do in the Safe House?[/b]
[list]
[*] Inventory management: Here players can organize their gear, prepare mission loadouts, upgrade weapons and armor.
[*] The place allows you to rest and regenerate health.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057663/404897b93027d50480cbf5e0642de3a700be9e5b.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057663/6df8557a468d1038e396f618635c9fc7c75105ac.jpg[/img]
The Safe House will be a location players can access after completing a given mission. Its appearance will change depending on the game progress.

In the previous devlog, we presented models representing health, shield, and oxygen, which can be found during the journey on Tarvos.

[h3][b]The player will need to pay attention to 3 parameters:[/b][/h3]
[list]
[*] Armor – The durability of the suit, which can be upgraded over time. If the armor is at a good level, it prevents the decrease of vital stats.
[*] Health – Decreases when the armor is broken; losing health equals death and loss of level progress.
[*] Oxygen – The oxygen level affects the reduction of health, regardless of how strong the armor is. Lack of oxygen negates everything.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057663/17402a7b79f1bc8559080a9606bdd28983b3ecc3.png[/img]

[h3]That’s all for today![/h3]

notes.title: Devlog #4 – Suggest a name for new boss
notes.content:
Hi there!

We know it’s been a while since our last update — we disappeared off the radar for a bit, but not without reason. Over the past few months, we’ve been hard at work on Tarvos Desolation, and today we’re finally ready to share the results of that work with you.

This time around, there’s less narrative, but more solid information. We’ve prepared a breakdown of the newest features, models, and improvements we’re working on for upcoming versions of the game. If you’re waiting for fresh news about monsters, gear, and mechanics – this post is for you.

[h1]New Monster:[/h1]

We're planning a new boss – a mutated version of one of the existing creatures. It's still early in development and we're gathering ideas, but we already know it'll be a tough opponent with unique attacks and a dark backstory. We're also thinking about a name – if you have any ideas, feel free to share them on our Discord or any of the social platforms where we're active!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057663/20e4d3ca98c94bb13e449c30a1538a81fcbece76.png[/img]

[h1]Grenade Launcher:[/h1]

As part of our ongoing weapon system work, we’ve added a new grenade launcher model to the arsenal. It’s still an early version, but we wanted to share the current look — compact, straightforward, and built for functionality.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057663/66a47b342ab41df9af72aa32c02858f6dfd6f7e5.png[/img]

[h3]Key features:[/h3]

[i]Compact build:[/i] The model appears solid but not excessively heavy — ideal for close-quarters combat and tight spaces.

[i]Top detail:[/i] The top part includes a sight or mounting system — small, but enough to give the weapon a tactical look.

[i]Clear segmentation:[/i] Three main components stand out: the body, barrel, and rear section. Each has been sculpted separately using different shades of gray, making it easier for players to read its shape during fast-paced gameplay.

[i]Neutral color scheme:[/i] The muted tones (graphite, gray, black) suggest a military purpose and fit well with the rest of our gear.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057663/1000562627e74a15b07a8f9fcf5d22df591a9774.png[/img]

[h3]Function in-game:[/h3]

We’re not revealing full combat details just yet — but this will be a high-impact weapon, designed to deal with groups of enemies and environmental cover. It’ll shine in scenarios where raw firepower matters more than precision.

[h1]Exoskeleton:[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057663/ad237aa283c1f5a026b911ac8a2e67a18141be2d.png[/img]

[h3]Key features:[/h3]

[i]Modular design:[/i] Each component of the exoskeleton has been designed to allow for mission-specific customization.

[i]Reinforced limbs:[/i] Thick joints and mechanical support systems provide extra strength and durability. This suit is useful in both close combat and heavy lifting scenarios.

[i]Tactical details:[/i] Various mounts are visible on the torso, allowing for integration of targeting systems, shields, or extra gear.

[i]Neutral, military color palette:[/i] Dark tones dominate — graphite, gray, matte black. The exoskeleton blends in with other equipment and doesn’t stand out in combat zones.

[h1]Weapon Handling:[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057663/10f8a55028167f84fb5cc893bf822ae1d7a240c8.png[/img]

We aimed to enhance immersion through subtle but crucial changes to how the character interacts with weapons. We believe that weapon handling affects not only visual appeal but also how the combat mechanics feel — players should feel the difference between a heavy grenade launcher and a rapid-firing laser rifle.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057663/b55ca67ba79fed3e78db9113b2513ab8196a3400.png[/img]

[h1]Join the Community![/h1]

Your feedback is incredibly important to us. Follow our journey on social media and join the conversation on our Discord server — connect with other players, share your thoughts, and get exclusive updates.

[i]Until the next update.

— Tarvos Research Team[/i]
